From a botanical point of view, the fruits can be classiﬁed into:
1. Fleshy fruits (derived from a single ﬂower):
• Drupe: Fleshy pericarp that surrounds a seed with a woody shell.
-
Apricot, plum, peach.
-
Avocado, mango, sour cherry, cherry.
-
Aggregates (strawberry, raspberry, blackberry).
-
Rowanberries: Part of the ﬂower is the ﬂoral receptacle (peduncle).
-
Apple, pear, quince.
• Berries: Fleshy fruits with tiny seeds freely arranged in the pulp.
– Grape, blueberry, bananas, papaya, cherimoya.
– Date, watermelon, melon, currant, kiwi.
– Hesperidium or citrus fruits (orange, lemon, tangerine, lime).
2. Compound ﬂeshy fruits (derived from an inﬂorescence):
• Sorosis: Pineapple.
• Syconium: Fig.

Nutritional components of fruits
Energy
